statement: For the linear function $g$, $g(2) = 7$ and $g(g(2)) = 22$. What is the value of $g(10)$?

choices.misconception: I found the slope 3 correctly but wrote $g(10) = 3 \cdot 10 = 30$ and left out the $+1$.
I assumed $g$ is proportional because $g(2) = 7$, so I used $g(x) = \dfrac{7}{2}x$ and got $g(10) = 35$.
I read $g(g(2))$ as $g(2 \cdot 2) = g(4) = 22$, so I got a slope of $7.5$ and $g(10) = 7 + 8(7.5) = 67$.

hints: Since $g(2) = 7$, the expression $g(g(2))$ is the same as $g(7)$.
You now know two points on the graph of $g$: $(2, 7)$ and $(7, 22)$. Find the slope and intercept.
The slope is $\dfrac{22 - 7}{7 - 2} = 3$, so $g(x) = 3x + b$ with $3(2) + b = 7$.

solutions.reliable: Because $g(2) = 7$, we have $g(7) = 22$. The slope is $\dfrac{22 - 7}{7 - 2} = 3$. From $g(2) = 3(2) + b = 7$ we get $b = 1$, so $g(x) = 3x + 1$ and $g(10) = 31$. Check: $g(2) = 7$ and $g(7) = 22$.
solutions.elegant: From $x = 7$ to $x = 10$ is $3$ more units at slope $3$, so $g(10) = 22 + 9 = 31$.
